headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: MemMachine’s MCP/API outputs can feed Semantic Kernel’s writable, networked orchestration path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, while Semantic Kernel consumes MCP servers and plugins. That creates a default content bridge where MemMachine outputs can be treated as tool input by Semantic Kernel. The pair lacks documented provenance filtering, so prompt-like content in MemMachine context can steer Semantic Kernel.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is routed into Semantic Kernel via MCP or plugin calls
IF Semantic Kernel parses MemMachine-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all MemMachine outputs before passing them onward
Insert a manual review step before Semantic Kernel tool execution
Restrict Semantic Kernel plugins to a fixed allowlist
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents unless needed
requires-engineering: add instruction/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and Semantic Kernel reads files, writes files, and sends data to broad networked model providers. If MemMachine context is forwarded into Semantic Kernel, sensitive user data can leave the local boundary through provider APIs. The profiles do not show a default isolation barrier.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is forwarded into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins
IF Semantic Kernel uses a remote model provider for that session
mitigations: Minimize MemMachine context before handoff
Redact personal facts from shared prompts
Use a local-only model provider for the Semantic Kernel session
Separate credentials for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can connect through an MCP Server, and Semantic Kernel can write files and use MCP servers. Even though MemMachine itself does not advertise filesystem write, the pair can overlap on shared mutable resources through application-defined files or MCP-backed state. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so concurrent writes can conflict.
conditions: IF both agents target the same application-defined files or shared memory store
IF Semantic Kernel instances run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Turn off shared memory-store writes for one agent
Use file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit conversational context and preferences, and Semantic Kernel is a multi-agent orchestrator that can act on plugin outputs. If Semantic Kernel treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. The profiles show no built-in verification step between them.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses MemMachine output as an input to planning or tool calls
IF no verification or human review step is inserted
mitigations: Require citations or source links before actioning outputs
Add a second-pass verifier agent
Limit MemMachine to suggestion-only mode
Log and review high-impact actions
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and preferences, while Semantic Kernel handles application context and may send prompts to external model providers. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: shared handling of user data with different logging/retention assumptions. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair.
conditions: IF the deployment subjects MemMachine data to Semantic Kernel provider logging
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two agents
mitigations: Document retention for both agents
Avoid sending regulated data to remote providers
Align deletion workflows across systems
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
requires-engineering: harmonize compliance controls end-to-end
